# Read-Back: Thanksgiving for Eight with One Oven

A complete Thanksgiving dinner for 8 people—roast turkey, gravy, stuffing, green bean casserole, mashed potatoes, and warm dinner rolls—must be ready to serve together at 6 PM (18:00). The kitchen has one oven, four burners (though the recipe emphasizes the oven as the critical bottleneck), and two cooks working together. The turkey dominates the schedule: it must come to room temperature 40 minutes before seasoning, then roast for 3 hours; while it rests for 40 minutes, the sides bake one after another in the newly available oven. The stuffing goes in as soon as the turkey comes out, the green bean casserole follows after the turkey has rested about 10 minutes, and the rolls warm last. Mashed potatoes are peeled and boiled while the turkey roasts, then held warm on the back burner. Gravy is made immediately from the pan drippings as the turkey emerges. Everything must finish by 18:00 so it arrives at the table hot and together.
